gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-canadian-ab: One-nib swagger, with cut-open terminals that let each counter flow outward. Noto Sans Canadian Aboriginal steps in with open curve ends, a quieter sans that lets the heading's uniform bar thickness carry the line.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-new-tai-lue: Gabarito draws every letter like a bent paperclip, with no thick-thin shifts and terminals cut open. And Noto Sans New Tai Lue, a plain sans with cupped round letters, softens that wire-like line into something friendly.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-nko: Noto Sans NKo is a modern sans-serif with see-through c openings, placed beneath Gabarito and its uniform-gauge, one-nib strokes. Paragraphs should move along easily, with hardly any friction from line to line.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoine: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans NKo Unjoined, a sans-serif with wide openings on small letters. But Gabarito, with its pipe-cleaner feel, hands over to text that reads smoothly across many lines.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-old-south-a: Pure one-nib attitude from Gabarito, with constant-width arms and legs; Noto Sans Old South Arabian lets curves stop before turning inward. Reading moves along cleanly, unhurried, line after line.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-philosopher: Gabarito looks like bent wire, round letters drawn with one nib. It grabs attention in large display lines, while Philosopher, a plain sans with soft thickness shifts and daylight inside its curves, does the steady reading work.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-pt-sans: Expressive is the mood of Gabarito, flat as fineliner ink. It is best at making a headline stand out, while PT Sans, a sans-serif with open arcs for its c forms, is best at carrying text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-quattrocento-sans: Pencil-straight and unfussy: Gabarito never thickens or thins, while Quattrocento Sans keeps its c from collapsing into an o. Their shared strength is a crisp, uncluttered look on the page.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-red-hat-text: One-nib charm from Gabarito, with Red Hat Text, a sans at technical-pen line weight, whose curvy letters feel unclamped. The headline leads and the text follows, loose and unhurried.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-rosario: Gabarito sets down a plain stripe of constant ink, terminals cut open. Rosario, a plain sans whose c ends never turn inward, then carries paragraphs forward with an easy, unbroken flow.
